notes:
Overall a solid implementation with clean code and good TypeScript usage, but several architectural and constraint violations exist. 

Architectural issues: (1) CommentService receives callback functions (getTaskTitle, getUserName) that are closures over UserService and TaskService instances — this is a direct service-to-service coupling disguised as dependency injection. It violates Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) because the comment service is effectively calling into other services synchronously at publish time, not via the event bus. The event payload could simply carry the needed data, or the comment service could publish with only IDs and let the notification service resolve names via its own cached state from prior events. (2) NotificationService maintains a taskAssignees cache built from events, which is a reasonable pattern, but it means comment notifications only fire if a task.assigned event was previously received — no comment notification fires for unassigned tasks, and no notification goes to other project members (only the assignee). This is a design limitation. (3) The isForwardTransition allows same-status transitions (indexOf newStatus >= indexOf oldStatus) in update(), meaning you can set todo->todo which is fine, but changeStatus() correctly short-circuits on same status. Minor inconsistency.

Constraint violations: (1) Rule 1 violated — CommentService directly invokes getTaskTitle and getUserName closures that reach into TaskService and UserService. (2) The task.assigned event payload doesn't include enough data for NotificationService to know the previous assignee when reassignment happens, so stale taskAssignees cache could send notifications to the wrong user. (3) router.ts imports all service types directly, which is acceptable as it's the API layer, not a service calling another service. (4) All services are in their own files — Rule 6 satisfied. (5) No npm dependencies — Rule 5 satisfied. (6) Forward-only transitions implemented correctly in changeStatus; the update() method also enforces it which is good.

Completeness: All CRUD operations present for all entities. Events task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added all published. NotificationService subscribes to all three. Demo script exercises all features. markAsRead endpoint present. GET /tasks requires projectId query param which is a minor API design choice but limits discoverability. No getById for notifications. DELETE member uses request body which is non-standard for REST but functional.

Code quality: Clean, idiomatic TypeScript, good use of Map stores, proper error handling with try/catch in router, consistent response patterns, good use of randomUUID, ISO timestamps. The router is long but well-organized. Minor: isForwardTransition uses >= which allows same-status in update path unnecessarily.
